notes: Perfect agreement on human AMD sample analysis (C16, C17, C97). Both identify lack of quantification, inadequate sample characterization, and need for patient clinical data as reasons for uncertainty.

Complete claim overlap (C61-C64) on temporal analysis showing vascular changes precede neural disruption. LLM finds temporal sequence convincing; peer reviewers request additional controls to exclude primary tissue effects and question whether current data fully rules out confounds.

High overlap on sFLT-1 localization claims (C18-C22, C96). LLM accepts complementary techniques as sufficient; peer reviewers raise concerns about inconsistent staining patterns between figures and incomplete characterization of expression domains.

Strong overlap on antibody blockade experiments (C29-C32, C98). LLM finds statistical significance and controls convincing; peer reviewers express philosophical concerns about reproducibility of injection-based experiments and technical skill requirements.

Good overlap on overall significance and convergent evidence (C66, C67, C70, C81, C92, C103). Both agree the study is compelling and clinically important, with convergent evidence from multiple approaches supporting spontaneous CNV/RAP models.

Moderate overlap on AAV-shRNA approach (C40, C41, C44-C46). Both acknowledge this as one of three convergent approaches. Peer reviewers note individual weaknesses but accept overall convergent evidence as compelling.

Good overlap on transgenic model phenotypes (C50-C55, C100-C101). LLM finds penetrance data and molecular validation sufficient; peer reviewers emphasize importance of these models but request quantification of neovascularization events per retina to assess frequency and reproducibility.

Partial overlap on VEGF-A measurement (C29, C30, C38). LLM accepts ELISA and binding assay data; peer reviewers question whether ELISA measures only free VEGF or includes sFLT-1-bound VEGF, requesting in vitro validation.

Moderate overlap on CNV characterization in transgenic models (C50-C55). LLM accepts histological and angiographic evidence; peer reviewers raise major concerns about CNV quantification methodology, lack of vascular-specific staining, and inability to distinguish CNV from fluid leakage.

Moderate overlap on cell-type specificity and diffusion barriers (C74, C75). Both express uncertainty about functional implications. Peer reviewers specifically question whether sFLT-1 from one cell type could compensate via diffusion, challenging the explanation for distinct phenotypes.

Partial overlap on shRNA knockdown validation (C39, C40, C99). LLM accepts Western blot and IHC confirmation; peer reviewers request demonstration that membrane FLT-1 is unaffected and question extent of sFLT-1 reduction across retinal layers.

Small overlap on PlGF measurements (C33, C38). LLM accepts PlGF data as ruling out PlGF involvement; peer reviewers question whether ELISA measures free PlGF versus sFLT-1-bound PlGF and request explanation for unchanged PlGF levels.

Small overlap on CNV frequency in transgenic models (C52-C55). LLM accepts reported penetrance; peer reviewers note CNV occurs in control eyes at lower incidence and request discussion of why this happens, raising questions about specificity.

Small overlap on convergent evidence and mechanistic conclusions (C70, C81). Both agree that multiple independent approaches provide compelling evidence for sFLT-1's critical role in maintaining photoreceptor avascular privilege.

Small overlap on molecular validation in transgenic models (C57-C59). LLM accepts decreased sFLT-1 and increased VEGF-A as validation; peer reviewers request VEGF protein IHC to demonstrate spatial localization changes and more complete characterization.

Minimal overlap on differential expression patterns (C23, C24). LLM finds polarized distribution well-documented; peer reviewers question inconsistent staining patterns between figures as part of broader localization concerns.
Minimal overlap on cell-type specificity validation (C48, C49). Both accept that mT/mG reporter mice demonstrate appropriate Cre expression patterns in RPE and photoreceptor-specific lines.

Minimal overlap on Cre-mediated deletion approach (C47). LLM accepts conditional deletion strategy; peer reviewers request critical control experiment with mTmG mice to determine recombination efficiency and location for subretinal Cre plasmid injection.

Minimal overlap on RAP lesion characterization (C56). LLM accepts histological evidence; peer reviewers request vascular-specific staining, noting impossibility of confirming vascular changes based solely on H&E stains.
Claims C25, C27, C28 about functional interpretation of polarized distribution and vascular balance appear only in LLM results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
Claims C68, C69 about VEGF-A overexpression being insufficient and importance of sFLT-1:VEGF-A ratio appear only in LLM results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
Claims C77-C79 about AAV knockdown producing less CNV and potential loxP insertion artifacts appear only in LLM results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
Claim C83 about potential Wnt signaling confound in photoreceptor knockdown appears only in LLM results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

Claims C87-C90, C102 about broader implications, translational impact, and therapeutic applications appear only in LLM results. These speculative claims about future impact were not addressed in peer review.
Claim C60 about molecular validation appears only in peer review results (requesting VEGF protein localization). LLM addressed related claims C57-C59 but not C60 specifically.
